text:
The loudest Bruins story isn't a goal. Pavel Zacha's name has been all over the trade wires since Detroit sent Dylan Larkin to Montreal, with reports linking him to Minnesota as Bill Guerin hunts for a center. Zacha centers Boston's top line with David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka, so any move there reshapes the lineup, not just the depth chart.

On the ice, Elias Lindholm has finally given Boston what it paid for. He scored four times against Washington, has 11 points in his last 10 games (8.3 expected), and his line with Casey Mittelstadt and rookie James Hagens is getting 55% of the expected goals at 5v5.

The standings flatter them a bit. Boston is 15-8-1 with 31 points, but our expected points say about 26.6, a luck gap of 4.4. The goaltending is the reason: they have allowed almost 10 fewer goals than the chances deserved, and Michael DiPietro is at .926 over his last five starts while Jeremy Swayman shares the net. The team's 5v5 share is a modest 53%, carried by Charlie McAvoy and Hampus Lindholm (64% of the expected goals together).

The worrying part is home ice. As 98.5 The Sports Hub's Ty Anderson noted, the 4-2 loss to Winnipeg made it four losses in five at TD Garden for the first time since December 2016. Our numbers still put them at 77% to make the playoffs.
headline: Lindholm wakes up, Zacha's name gets loud
